metadata.case_name: SZE PING CHUI v. LAU CHING WAI

injuries.description: At the Eye Clinic, the Plaintiff was found to have a ruptured left eyeball with a 5mm full thickness linear corneal laceration at the visual axis and cataract and the lens was also damaged.
source: At the Eye Clinic, the Plaintiff was found to have a ruptured left eyeball with a 5mm full thickness linear corneal laceration at the visual axis and cataract and the lens was also damaged.
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration without prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

injuries.description: The crystalline lens had been removed by surgery and replaced by an intra-ocular lens (pseudophakic).
source: the crystalline lens had been removed by surgery and replaced by an intra-ocular lens

injuries.description: Despite the treatment, the Plaintiff has residual corneal scar at his left eye.
source: Despite the treatment, the Plaintiff has residual corneal scar at his left eye.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of conjunctiva or corneal abrasion without mention of foreign body

manifestations.description: Blurring of vision of his left eye
Occasional "light reflection" in the left eye
Occasional discomfort and photophobia in the left eye
Best-corrected visual acuity was 0.3 which corresponded to 65% loss of the left eye vision
Dr Cheung concluded the Plaintiff is suffering from 67% permanent disability in the left eye which is equivalent to 17% disability of the whole visual system and 16% disability of the whole person

treatments_received: Urgent operation to repair the cornea, removal of the damaged lens and implantation of intro-ocular lens performed on the same day of accident
Follow-up treatment at the United Christian Hospital and the Hong Kong Eye Hospital
Referral to the Hong Kong Eye Hospital in May 1999 for consideration of penetrating keratoplasty surgery

losses.description: Residual corneal scar and resulting reduced vision, blurring, occasional light reflection, occasional discomfort and photophobia; assessed permanent disability in the left eye (67% of left eye; 17% of whole visual system; 16% of whole person).

comparable_cases.injury_description: Total blindness in his left eye (which amounted to 24% permanent impairment of the whole visual system)
